about.name: Sharif Rayhan
about.title: Full Stack Developer & ML Research Enthusiast
about.tagline: Crafting scalable web applications with NextJS & FastAPI while exploring the future of AI and multimodal systems.
about.summary: Computer Science & Engineering graduate from the University of Dhaka with a strong focus on full stack web development using React, Next.js, FastAPI, and modern backend architectures. Passionate about building clean, scalable, and high-performance applications that solve real-world problems. Alongside software engineering, deeply interested in machine learning research, particularly multimodal large language models and video understanding systems, aligned with ongoing thesis work on long-video question answering. Currently seeking entry-level software engineering opportunities where I can contribute, learn, and grow as a full stack developer and AI-focused engineer.

education.degree: Bachelor of Science in Computer Science and Engineering

projects.title: CSEDU Department Website
projects.description: Collaborative project to develop the official website of the University of Dhaka CSE department featuring academic resources, announcements, meetings, and event management.

Developed frontend pages and integrated them with backend APIs.
Built scalable backend services using FastAPI and Next.js.

projects.title: Marketplace Web Application
projects.description: Flask-based backend system with modular architecture and REST APIs for scalable marketplace operations.

Applied modular backend architecture for scalability and maintainability.

projects.title: Bookly - Android Application

projects.title: NetConnect - Terminal-Based Group Chat System
projects.description: Multi-user real-time terminal chat application with custom networking protocol and access-controlled group communication.
highlights: Implemented real-time multi-user messaging using socket programming.
Designed group creation and approval-based access control.
Developed a custom protocol for efficient communication.

research.title: CATS: Curvature-Adaptive Temporal Suppression for Long-Video Question Answering
research.description: A novel budget-aware frame selection method for multimodal large language models addressing inefficiencies in long-video question answering caused by suboptimal frame sampling.
highlights: Introduces curvature-adaptive temporal suppression to reduce redundant frames.
Preserves short-term salient events and long-range contextual information.
Improves efficiency for multimodal LLM-based long-video QA systems.
